questions.question:
다음 글의 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?

B: Hi, Julie. You look (A) [worried / happy]. Can I help you?
G: Yes, I'm looking for my phone. I think I lost it.
B: Your phone will (B) [ring / stop] when I call. I'm calling you now.
G: Ah, here it is! Thank you for (C) [helping / disturbing] me.
B: You're welcome.
questions.explanation: Julie는 걱정해 보이고(worried), 전화가 울릴 때(ring) 찾을 수 있으며, 도와줘서(helping) 감사합니다.

options: The announcement made by the principal about the school schedule
The gathering of club members to play games after school
The result of using the new food trays with lines
The situation where students refused to eat lunch
The increased amount of food waste in the cafeteria
questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ It이 가리키는 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?

The members of Warm Hearts gathered to solve this problem. We thought that adding lines to food trays would be helpful. Students could look at the lines and take the right amount of food.
Our school principal liked this idea, so he changed the food trays in the cafeteria. ⓐ It was a success! The new trays reduced a large amount of food waste!
questions.explanation: ⓐ It은 새로운 식판 라인 시스템을 사용한 결과(새로운 식판이 많은 양의 음식물 쓰레기를 줄였다는 것)를 가리킵니다.

options: the noise level in the area had to be strictly controlled
more lights were essential for the safety of people
the traffic flow should be changed to avoid heavy traffic
more security cameras were needed to check the students
the sensors on the existing lights needed to be removed
questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

After we solved this problem at our school, we started to look for problems in our community. We found out that some roads around our school were very dark at night. We all agreed that _____________________________________________. With the help of a teacher, we put up lights with sensors around the neighborhood. Now all our neighbors feel safer than before!
questions.explanation: 도로가 어둡다는 문제를 발견했고, 센서가 있는 조명을 설치했으므로, 사람들의 안전을 위해 더 많은 불이 필요하다는 것에 동의했습니다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ~ 중 어법상 틀린 부분을 찾아 옳게 고친 것은?

Hello, everyone! I'm Yuna, and I'm the leader of Warm Hearts, a club at our school. Our club solves some problems in our school and our community over the past few year. I want sharing our stories.
One day, our school principal announced, "Our students often take too much food and wastes it at lunchtime. Can how we reduce food waste?"
questions.explanation: "I want sharing"은 "I want to share"로 수정되어야 합니다. want 다음에는 to부정사가 와야 합니다.

questions.question:
다음 대화를 읽고 추론할 수 있는 내용을 <보기>에서 모두 고른 것은?

W: Welcome to the Happy Animal Shelter. Can I help you?
B: Yes. I'm here to volunteer.
W: Can I have your name, please?
B: I'm Jinho. I love dogs, so I want to take care of them.
W: That's great! I'll introduce our puppies first.
B: They're so cute. What should I do to help?
W: While we clean the cage, take these puppies for a walk, please.
B: Okay. I'm excited to spend some time with them!
W: I'm glad. Thank you for volunteering!

<보기>
a. This is Jinho's first time volunteering at this shelter.
b. Jinho will walk the puppies while the staff cleans the cages.
c. Jinho has a lot of experience in taking care of animals.
d. The shelter is moving to a new place because there are too many dogs.
questions.explanation: a는 맞습니다(스태프가 강아지들을 소개하겠다고 말함). b도 맞습니다(케이지를 청소하는 동안 강아지들을 산책시키도록 지시). c는 경험이 많다는 언급이 없으므로 틀립니다. d는 대피소 이동에 대한 언급이 없으므로 틀립니다.

questions.question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

주어진 문장: We came up with an idea to put lines on the food trays.

원문:
One day, our school principal announced, "Our students often take too much food and waste it at lunchtime. How can we reduce food waste?" ( )
The members of Warm Hearts gathered to solve this problem. ( ) Students could look at the lines and take the right amount of food. ( )
Our school principal liked this idea, so he changed the food trays in the cafeteria. ( ) It was a success! ( ) The new trays reduced a large amount of food waste!
questions.explanation: Warm Hearts 회원들이 문제를 해결하기 위해 모였다는 설명 다음에, 그들이 식판에 라인을 넣는 아이디어를 생각해냈다는 내용이 와야 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)와 의미가 같도록 문장을 바꿔 쓸 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Have you ever used a digital kiosk before? You may think it's easy. (A) But some people have trouble using kiosks.

→ But it is difficult ______ some people ______ use kiosks.
questions.explanation: "have trouble using"은 "it is difficult for (사람) to (동사)" 구문으로 바뀝니다. 따라서 "it is difficult for some people to use kiosks"가 정답입니다.

options: Local residents work together to collect trash and keep the streets clean.
The local government hires workers to construct new buildings
Students are required to attend classes about environmental protection
People gather to sell used items and donate the money to people in need
Volunteers plant trees to make the streets look more colorful
questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

B: Good morning, Soye! What are you doing?
G: Hi, Ben. I'm trying to put up a poster, but it's not easy.
B: Can I help you? I can hold it for you.
G: Sure! Thank you for lending a hand.
B: You're welcome. What is this poster for?
G: It's for the Community Cleanup.
B: What is the Community Cleanup?
G: It's a volunteer activity. ____________________.
B: That's a good idea! Can I join?
G: Of course! It is open to everyone.
questions.explanation: "Community Cleanup"은 지역 주민들이 함께 쓰레기를 수거하고 거리를 깨끗하게 유지하는 자원봉사 활동입니다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

The members of Warm Hearts (A) [gathered / gathering] to solve this problem. We thought (B) [that / what] adding lines to food trays would be helpful. Students could look at the lines and take the right amount of food.
Our school principal liked this idea, so he changed the food trays in the cafeteria. It was a success! The new trays reduced a (C) [large / largely] amount of food waste!
questions.explanation: (A) gathered는 과거 동사로 회원들이 모였다는 의미. (B) that은 think의 목적어로 사용. (C) large는 형용사로 amount를 수식합니다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 우리말 (A)와 일치하도록 <조건>에 맞춰 영작했을 때, 8번째 올 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

After we solved this problem at our school, we started to look for problems in our community.
(A) 우리는 학교 주변의 어떤 길들이 밤에 매우 어둡다는 것을 알아냈다.
We all agreed that the roads needed more lights. With the help of a teacher, we put up lights with sensors around the neighborhood. Now all our neighbors feel safer than before!

<조건>
- 아래 주어진 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 사용하여 문장을 완성할 것
- out / were / school / that / dark / roads / found / we / very / some / around / at / our / night
questions.explanation: 문장 순서: We found out that some roads around our school were very dark at night. 8번째 단어는 "some"입니다.

options: I enjoy doing yoga every morning.
Doing homework is important for students.
Thank you for doing me a favor.
She is doing her best to win the game.
My hobby is doing magic tricks.
questions.question:
다음 대화의 밑줄 친 ⓐ와 쓰임이 같은 것은?

G: Hey, Junsu. What are you ⓐ doing?
B: Hi, Amy. There is a problem with my bike. I'm trying to fix it.
G: Can I help you? I'll hold the bike.
B: Sure, thank you.
questions.explanation: ⓐ doing은 "What are you doing?" (현재 진행 중인 행동)으로 사용됩니다. 4번 "She is doing her best"도 현재 진행형으로 같은 쓰임입니다.

options: He is kind and thoughtful because he helps before being asked.
He only helped after Ms. Lee asked him to open the door.
He is a student assistant who helps staff members.
He only opened the door because Ms. Lee said no to his help with the books.
Jihun and Ms. Lee planned to meet here.
questions.question:
[대화]
B: Hello, Ms. Lee. Can I help you? Your hands are full.
W: Oh, hi, Jihun. Yes, please. Can you open the door for me?
B: No problem. I can also carry the books for you.
W: Thank you! Please put them over there.
B: Okay. Is there anything else?
W: That's it. Thank you so much for helping me.
B: You're welcome. Have a nice day, Ms. Lee!

다음 대화의 Jihun에 관해 추론할 수 있는 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: Jihun이 Ms. Lee의 손이 가득 찬 것을 보고 스스로 도움을 제시했으며, Ms. Lee가 문을 열어달라고 요청하기 전에 이미 '도와줄 수 있다'고 말했다. 따라서 그는 요청받기 전에 도움을 주는 친절하고 생각이 깊은 사람이다.

questions.question:
[지문]
After we solved this problem at our school, we started to (A) [give up / look for] problems in our community. We found out that some roads around our school were very dark at night. We all (B) [accepted / denied] that the roads needed more lights. With the help of a teacher, we put up lights with sensors around the neighborhood. Now all our neighbors feel more (C) [secure / unsafe] than before!

다음 글의 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: (A) 학교 문제를 해결한 후 지역사회의 문제를 '찾다'는 의미로 'look for'가 맞다. (B) 도로에 더 많은 조명이 필요하다는 것을 '인정했다'는 의미로 'accepted'가 맞다. (C) 이제 이웃들이 이전보다 더 '안전감을 느낀다'는 의미로 'secure'가 맞다.

questions.question:
[지문]
Have you ever (A) [use / used] a digital kiosk before? You may think it's easy. But some people have trouble using kiosks.
To help them, we volunteered as digital guides at the community center. We explained every step of ordering: starting an order, (B) [choose / choosing] from the menu, and paying.
After the class, people said, "Now we feel more (C) [comfortable / comfortably] with kiosks. Thank you so much!" We felt very proud.

다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: (A) 'Have you ever'는 현재완료 형태이므로 'used'(과거분사)가 맞다. (B) '시작하다, 메뉴에서 선택하다, 그리고 지불하다'에서 병렬 구조를 이루므로 동명사 'choosing'이 맞다. (C) 'feel'은 감각동사이므로 형용사 'comfortable'이 보어로 와야 한다.

questions.question:
[지문]
Hello, everyone! I'm Yuna, and I'm the leader of Warm Hearts, a club at our school. Our club has (A) ignored some problems in our school and our community over the past few years. I want to (B) share our stories.
One day, our school principal (C) announced, "Our students often take too (D) little food and waste it at lunchtime. How can we (E) reduce food waste?"

다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것들로 짝지어진 것은?
questions.explanation: (A) 'ignored'는 '무시했다'는 의미인데, 문맥상 클럽이 문제들을 주목했고 해결했으므로 'addressed'와 같은 단어가 적절하다. (D) 'take too little'은 '너무 적게 가져가다'는 의미인데, 낭비 문제를 언급하므로 'too much'가 적절하다.

questions.question:
[지문]
Have you ever used a digital kiosk before? You may think it's easy. But some people have trouble using kiosks. ①To help them, we volunteered as digital guides at the community center. ②People are worried that they might lose their jobs because kiosks are replacing human cashiers. ③We explained every step of ordering: starting an order, choosing from the menu, and paying. ④After the class, people said, "Now we feel more comfortable with kiosks. ⑤Thank you so much!"

다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
questions.explanation: 글의 전체 흐름은 자원봉사자들이 사람들을 도와 키오스크 사용법을 배우게 했다는 내용이다. 'People are worried that they might lose their jobs because kiosks are replacing human cashiers.'라는 문장은 글의 주요 내용과 무관한 외부 정보이므로 전체 흐름을 방해한다.

options: He is explaining how mobile phones work.
He wants to find the phone by listening to the sound.
He wants to talk to her on the phone right now.
He is checking if the phone is broken.
He tells her to buy a new phone with a loud sound.
questions.question:
[대화]
B: Hi, Julie. You look worried. Can I help you?
G: Yes, I'm looking for my phone. I think I lost it.
B: (A) Your phone will ring when I call. I'm calling you now.
G: Ah, here it is! Thank you for helping me.
B: You're welcome.

다음 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: B는 Julie의 폰에 전화를 걸어 울리는 소리를 통해 폰의 위치를 찾도록 돕고 있다. Julie가 '여기 있어요!'라고 하며 폰을 찾은 것으로 보아, B의 의도는 울리는 소리를 들음으로써 폰을 찾는 것이다.

questions.question:
[대화]
W: Welcome to the Happy Animal Shelter. Can I help you?
B: Yes. I'm here to volunteer.
W: Can I have your name, please?
B: I'm Jinho. I love dogs, so I want to take care of them.
W: That's great! I'll introduce our puppies first.
B: They're so cute. What should I do to help?
W: While we clean the cage, take these puppies for a walk, please.
B: Okay. (A) 나는 그들과 함께 약간의 시간을 보내게 되어 신나요!
W: I'm glad. Thank you for volunteering!

다음 대화의 밑줄 친 우리말 (A)와 일치하도록 <조건>에 맞춰 영작했을 때, 6번째 올 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

<조건>
- 아래 주어진 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 사용하여 문장을 완성할 것
- spend / with / I'm / to / excited / time / them / some
questions.explanation: 주어진 단어들을 사용하여 문장을 완성하면: 'I'm excited to spend some time with them.' 순서대로 I'm(1) excited(2) to(3) spend(4) some(5) time(6)이므로 6번째 단어는 'time'이다.

questions.question:
[지문]
After we solved this problem at our school, we started to look for problems in our community. We found out that some roads around our school were very dark at night. We all agreed that the roads needed more lights. With the help of a teacher, we put up lights with sensors around the neighborhood. Local residents often debated the design of the new lamp. Now all our neighbors feel safer than before!

다음 글의 ①~⑤ 중 문맥상 관계 없는 문장은?
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름은 지역사회의 문제를 찾아 조명을 설치하여 주민들이 더 안전함을 느끼게 되었다는 내용이다. 'Local residents often debated the design of the new lamp'라는 문장은 글의 긍정적인 흐름을 방해하는 불필요한 정보이므로 문맥상 관계가 없다.

questions.question:
[지문]
Have you ever used a digital kiosk before? You may think it's easy. But some people have trouble using kiosks. To (A) [help / disturb] them, we volunteered as digital guides at the community center. We explained every step of ordering: starting an order, choosing from the menu, and paying. After the class, people said, "Now we feel more (B) [comfortable / uncomfortable] with kiosks. Thank you so much!" We felt very (C) [proud / ashamed].

다음 글의 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: (A) 자원봉사자들이 사람들을 돕기 위해 활동했으므로 'help'가 맞다. (B) 수업 후 사람들이 키오스크에 대해 덜 불안해하고 더 편하다고 말했으므로 'comfortable'이 맞다. (C) 자신들의 도움이 효과적이었으므로 자원봉사자들은 'proud'(자랑스럽다)한 기분을 느낀다.
